evidence: instruction.md and all six notes are now in one consistent first-person requester voice: personal reasons motivate requirements ('I often paste a long one-line experiment' instruction.md:1; 'I run code I've pasted from all over the place' security.md:3; 'I keep the browser's network panel open while I debug' and 'My connection drops now and then' behaviour.md:13; 'I sometimes check things on my phone' ui.md:17), contractions throughout (it's, shouldn't, don't, won't, I've, I'd), varied sentence length, no bullets, numbered lists, shall/must tables or marketing gloss (grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|shall|comprehensive|intuitive across instruction+notes: zero hits; the only 'must' left is behaviour.md:13 'Restoring from an old page must not overwrite a newer save'). Commit 5e036ba0 removed the remaining spec register that would have been a voice shift between instruction.md and the notes: overview.md ('A long source line must remain editable' -> 'I often work on one very long line, so it needs to stay editable'), policy.md ('Use the public behaviour in these notes as the contract' -> 'These notes describe how I'll use the app'), security.md ('User-entered code runs in an isolated browser preview... must fail' -> 'I run code I've pasted... should fail') and integration.md ('must not require an install or build step' -> 'I won't run an install or build step'). Residual observations that do not reach a defect: integration.md:3,9,11 keeps terse imperative runtime facts (port, DB_PATH, symlink rule) under a first-person heading, which reads as a person's deployment notes rather than robotic prose; behaviour.md and ui.md are dense and edge-case precise (e.g. 'if my selection ends at the very start of the next line, leave that next line alone' ui.md:7), but each edge case is framed as the requester's own habit, so the text reads as a demanding developer, not an LLM checklist. Cross-check requested by the owner for rows 1/25/32/35 (whole task, not just flagged spots): (1) no 'must/contract/shall' acceptance register remains in any note; (25) no judge prompt, criterion or app_context directs any request off-machine; app_context.md:27 says 'No criterion needs any address outside this machine' and every http URL in tests/ is localhost:3000 or 127.0.0.1:3000; (32) every Stop/race leg now carries the same void-and-retry rule ('void, not a failure... up to two more times, and only if every attempt is void, fail'): cw_output_before_failure_kept judge.toml:254, cw_last_good_recovery :290, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work :308, cw_newer_run_supersedes :317; no other criterion depends on pressing Stop within a short window; (35) cw_save_reload_restart :344 now saves twice, restores through the app with the request recorded, re-reads current revision, full revision list and revision one after restart_app, then replays the recorded restore and requires no new revision; app_context.md:29 and functional/prompt.md:24 authorise that replay. Looser for the model? No grading criterion was relaxed; the note edits soften must->should/need wording but every softened requirement is still stated unambiguously and still graded (constraints gate for own editor, cw security criterion :326 for the loopback fetch, restart criterion for persistence). The only scope shift is stricter: restore idempotency must now hold across a real restart, which is covered by behaviour.md:9,13 (history survives restart; a repeated restore after it went through must add no revision) and is satisfiable by several designs (persisted request key or stale-base refusal). Not measured here: workload of the longer restart criterion and full judge runtime, which belong to other rows.
